findings.premise: The design covers all upstream requirements, decisions and non-goals.
findings.evidence: Analyzer retrieval and repository searches found this LLD and earlier variants. The persisted artifact contains only the routing rationale 'one cohesive cross-module story; no new subsystem'; its workflow log records stage events without storySpec or original requirements. The inline ac1–ac8 statements establish local criteria but do not establish upstream completeness. findings.action: Link or include the original storySpec, decisions and non-goals, then reconcile them with ac1–ac8.

findings.premise: Existing approval preserves review gates, non-overridable BUILD freshness, rejection clearing and write-once rangeBase.
findings.evidence: approveArtifactOwned checks BUILD freshness before processing overrideReview, enforces blocking and other-party reviews, preserves a non-empty priorBase, and deletes rejectedAt/rejectReason on approval. enforceCodeReviewGate returns stale-review before evaluating enforcement or overrides. [files: src/workflow/gates.ts, src/workflow/code-review/gate.ts]
findings.action: Preserve this ordering when inserting the presentation gate.

findings.premise: AMD approval uses a separate flat record, preserves approvedBy and treats resolved amendments as terminal; pending enumeration reads stored decision state.
findings.evidence: approveAmendment requires approvedBy and refuses prev.status !== 'pending'. transition preserves the immutable amendment fields. listPendingArtifacts checks AMD's top-level status; other artifacts are excluded when approvedAt or rejectedAt is non-empty. [files: src/workflow/amendments/store.ts, src/workflow/amendments/types.ts, src/workflow/pending.ts]
findings.action: Keep AMD transitions separate from envelope-based approval and preserve the pure pending scan.

findings.premise: Content hashing and cross-process writer ownership already exist, while presentation-token approval is new.
findings.evidence: contentVersionOf hashes markdown with SHA-256 and returns 16 hex characters; handleArtifactContent returns that version with the exact markdown read. withBuildWriter already provides canonical-path ownership, contention errors and dead-process recovery. Source searches found no production workflow.present, presentationToken, requireMatchingPresentation or withArtifactWriter implementation. [files: src/workflow/artifact-content.ts, src/workflow/approval-owner.ts, src/workflow/runners/build/standalone-record.ts, src/mcp/server.ts]
findings.action: Reuse contentVersionOf and generalize the existing ownership mechanism, retaining the same lock identity for BUILD writers.

findings.premise: The specified MCP mapping can complete version-bound presentation and subsequent token-bound approval while retaining its public response.
findings.evidence: InsrcPresentArgs accepts only documents:string[] and repo, and handleInsrcPresent returns JSON.stringify({ presented, notPending }) with string arrays. The design requires displayed contentVersion inputs and returns tokens internally, but specifies only 'recorded→presented' publicly. It defines neither how MCP obtains the displayed version nor how its approval caller receives the token. The review presenter also opens from the declaration without reading the tool result. [files: src/mcp/server.ts, vscode-plugin/src/chat/review-presenter.ts, vscode-plugin/src/chat/docs-review-client.ts, docs/standalone/enforce-approval-hard-gates-daemon-present-E20261103efd378ce/S001/LLD.md]
findings.action: Specify the complete MCP presentation handshake, displayed-version acknowledgement and token return or handoff mechanism, including interaction with IDE presentation and token supersession.

findings.premise: The batch approval signature can validate the distinct presentation token belonging to every explicitly listed artifact.
findings.evidence: recordPresentations returns a token per artifact, and requireMatchingPresentation requires stored-token equality. However, approveWorkflowTarget accepts artifactIds:string[] alongside only one presentToken:string. It cannot carry different tokens for two presented artifacts. Additionally, §2.8 explicitly adds only presentToken to the MCP approval schema, leaving artifactIds without a specified MCP input and forwarding path. [files: src/workflow/gates.ts, src/mcp/server.ts, src/mcp/daemon-stream.ts, docs/standalone/enforce-approval-hard-gates-daemon-present-E20261103efd378ce/S001/LLD.md]
findings.action: Define an artifact-to-token batch contract through the daemon request, MCP schema and forwarding handler, with exact coverage validation and tests using distinct tokens.

findings.premise: The client change inventory includes the complete VS Code approval forwarding path.
findings.evidence: DocsReviewClient.decide sends workflow.reviewDecision. ReviewDecisionRequest has no presentation token, and handleReviewDecision calls approveWorkflowTarget({ repoPath, artifactPath: jsonPath }), dropping any token supplied by a modified client. The design lists docs-review-client and handler-runtime but omits review-decision.ts and its request contract. A default-enabled gate therefore withholds this approval path. [files: vscode-plugin/src/chat/docs-review-client.ts, src/workflow/review-decision.ts, src/daemon/handler-runtime.ts, docs/standalone/enforce-approval-hard-gates-daemon-present-E20261103efd378ce/S001/LLD.md]
findings.action: Include ReviewDecisionRequest, its runtime input handling and approveWorkflowTarget forwarding in the token contract and client integration tests.

findings.premise: The writer inventory covers every production writer capable of replacing approval-relevant artifact state.
findings.evidence: handleSynthesize writes both finalized.renderedMd and finalized.renderedJson directly. patchTrackerMeta reads an entire envelope and writes it back; mutateEpicTrackerMeta independently does the same. These writers are absent from §3.6. They can replace content or overwrite presentation/consumption fields despite locks on the listed writers, invalidating the claimed serialization and no-lost-updates guarantee. [files: src/daemon/steps/workflow-step/phases/synthesize.ts, src/workflow/tracker/refs.ts, src/workflow/orchestrator.ts, src/workflow/runners/build/standalone-record.ts, docs/standalone/enforce-approval-hard-gates-daemon-present-E20261103efd378ce/S001/LLD.md]
findings.action: Extend the inventory to synthesis/re-authoring and tracker writers, define preservation or invalidation of presentation state, and coordinate BUILD persistence with the same lock.

findings.premise: Optional embedded presentation fields fit existing stored artifact and amendment shapes without requiring a data rewrite.
findings.evidence: Envelope readers tolerate additional metadata, and isAmendmentRecord checks required AMD fields without rejecting extra keys. Existing pending state remains determined by approval/rejection fields or AMD status. The design adequately describes artifact ownership of one current token, supersession and consumption in prose. No companion definitions or files are linked; an ERD is unnecessary for this embedded relationship, and no visual rendering verification is claimed. [files: src/workflow/gates.ts, src/workflow/amendments/types.ts, src/workflow/pending.ts, .insrc/artifacts/LLD-efd378ce6009d6b2-S001.json]
findings.action: Retain absent-field handling and fail closed for older pending records until presentation succeeds.

findings.premise: Extending BUILD_APPROVAL_IDENTITY_EXCLUSIONS is the correct mechanism for preventing presentation bookkeeping from invalidating BUILD review identity.
findings.evidence: canonicalReviewBuild copies metadata and deletes every key in BUILD_APPROVAL_IDENTITY_EXCLUSIONS before readOnce computes buildDigest. The current list contains approvedAt, rejectedAt, rejectReason and reviewOverride; other metadata and body fields remain fingerprinted. The proposed explicit additions fit this mechanism while retaining source and material BUILD identity. [files: src/workflow/code-review/input-fingerprint.ts, src/workflow/code-review/__tests__/input-fingerprint.test.ts, src/workflow/gates.ts]
findings.action: Implement the stated additions and retain regression coverage proving material changes still invalidate review.

findings.premise: Locking review publication with a fresh reread is sufficient to prevent an in-flight review from publishing against changed artifact content.
findings.evidence: reviewArtifactFile captures artifact, body and markdown before awaiting runReview, then constructs fixed.body and nextMd from that captured input. A fresh reread at final publication does not establish that the report reviewed the current body, and writing the captured result can overwrite intervening edits. The design specifies no reviewed-input version comparison or restart/error path for this race. [files: src/workflow/review/run-artifact.ts, src/daemon/steps/review-step/phases/findings.ts, src/daemon/steps/review-step/phases/verdicts.ts, docs/standalone/enforce-approval-hard-gates-daemon-present-E20261103efd378ce/S001/LLD.md]
findings.action: Bind review computation to an input snapshot and validate that snapshot under the publication lock; refuse or restart publication when it changed. Define handling for both JSON and markdown updates.

findings.premise: Each locally declared ac1–ac8 criterion has proposed proving tests supported by usable repository test harnesses.
findings.evidence: The acceptance table maps all eight criteria to unit, contract or integration scenarios. present-dispatch.test.ts provides a socket fake and exact public-shape assertions; docs-review-client.test.ts records IPC requests; tui.test.ts injects Services; method-class.test.ts compares registrations with runtime handlers; input-fingerprint.test.ts exercises approval exclusions and material changes. This verifies the test strategy's feasibility, not passage of unimplemented tests. findings.action: Retain these mappings and add explicit regressions for the MCP token handoff, distinct-token batch, reviewDecision forwarding, omitted writers and changed-input review publication identified above.

summary.prose: Token+contentVersion-bound present-before-approve in the daemon: workflow.present verifies the displayed contentVersion under a per-artifact lock and stamps a single-use token + presentedContentVersion; every approval request carries the token and is validated (token equality, unconsumed, TTL, current render === presentedContentVersion) under the same lock, then consumed. Re-presentation supersedes old tokens, so a stale view can never be approved. All approval-relevant writers serialize under the lock with fresh rereads. epicHash needs explicit artifactIds; overrides are token-gated; bookkeeping stays out of the BUILD fingerprint; stale-review stays non-overridable; AMD keeps approvedBy and terminal reject; document-less records get a version via deliveryEvidence; MCP keeps { presented, notPending }; TUI/IDE present on open.
